# Releasing

Releases are cut by the [Release workflow](workflows/release.yml). Nothing needs
to be bumped, tagged or written by hand.

## Cutting a release

1. Make sure everything you want to ship is merged into `master` and that
   **Hassfest** and **Validate** are green.
2. Go to **Actions → Release → Run workflow**.
3. Choose the bump:
   - **patch** — bug fixes (`2.4.2` → `2.4.3`)
   - **minor** — new sensors, new features (`2.4.2` → `2.5.0`)
   - **major** — breaking changes, e.g. renamed entities or requiring users to
     reconfigure
   - **none** — do not change the version, just publish what is already in
     `manifest.json`. Only for recovering a lost release; see below.
4. Optionally give it a **title**. Left blank it uses the version number;
   a one-line summary of the change reads better in the releases list.
5. Tick **prerelease** to ship it to beta testers only — see below.
6. Tick **draft** if you want to rewrite the notes before users see it.

The workflow then bumps the version in both
[manifest.json](../custom_components/willyweather/manifest.json) and
[const.py](../custom_components/willyweather/const.py) — the latter's
`VERSION` is what the integration reports as `sw_version` on the device page, so
the two must stay in lockstep. It commits them as `chore: bump version to
X.Y.Z`, tags that commit `vX.Y.Z`, and creates the GitHub release with notes
generated from the PRs and commits since the last one.

HACS picks the release up from that point. Because the tag points at the bump
commit, the version HACS installs always matches the tag.

## Recovering a lost release

If a release is deleted, or the workflow fails after pushing the bump commit,
the version in `manifest.json` has already moved on while no release exists for
it. Running the workflow again with a normal bump would spend a *second* version
number to fix a missing tag, and leave the first one permanently skipped.

Run it with bump **none** instead. It publishes the version already in
`manifest.json`: no bump, no commit, just the tag and the release.

Before running it, make sure the tag for that version either does not exist or
still points at the bump commit — if you deleted the release but not the tag,
the workflow reuses the tag; if you deleted both, it recreates it. A tag that
exists but points somewhere else is rejected, since that means the branch has
moved since and the tag no longer describes what would be shipped.

`none` is only for this situation. Publishing two different releases with the
same version number would leave HACS users on whichever they installed first,
with no way to tell them apart.

## Pre-releases

Ticking **prerelease** changes one thing: GitHub flags the release as a
pre-release and it is not marked *latest*. HACS only offers a pre-release to
users who have turned on beta versions for this repository (in HACS, open
**WillyWeather → ⋮ → Redownload**, then enable **Show beta versions**).
Everyone else keeps seeing the previous stable release and is never prompted.

The version number is a normal `X.Y.Z` — there is no `-beta` suffix. A
pre-release of `2.4.2` *is* `2.4.2`, in the tag and in `manifest.json`, so
promoting it later needs no new build:

> Open the release on GitHub → **Edit** → untick **Set as a pre-release**, tick
> **Set as the latest release** → **Update release**.

HACS then offers it to everyone, running byte-identical code to what the beta
testers were on. No second version, tag, commit or set of release notes.

If the beta turns out to be broken instead, just fix it and cut the next one.
`master` is already bumped to `2.4.2`, so the workflow will offer `2.4.3` next —
version numbers spent on abandoned betas are simply skipped, which costs
nothing.

Given this integration talks to a paid API against real weather stations, a beta
round is worth it for anything touching the coordinator's polling behaviour or
the API call pattern — a regression there costs users money, not just data.

## Prerequisites

The workflow pushes a commit, a tag and a release, so it needs write access:

- **Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions** must be
  *Read and write permissions*. The `permissions: contents: write` block in the
  workflow cannot grant more than the repository default allows.
- If `master` is protected, the `github-actions[bot]` actor needs to be allowed
  to push to it, or the bump commit will be rejected.

## Notes

- The release notes are generated by GitHub from merged pull request titles, so
  descriptive PR titles produce a usable changelog for free. A published
  release's notes can still be edited on GitHub afterwards.
- [CHANGELOG.md](../CHANGELOG.md) is maintained by hand and is the place for
  migration notes that a list of PR titles cannot convey — renamed entities,
  changed entity IDs, anything a user has to act on. Routine changes do not need
  an entry; the generated notes already cover those.
- Generated notes cover everything since the *previous tag*, and an abandoned
  pre-release still leaves a tag behind. So if `2.4.2` is cut as a beta and
  then dropped, `2.4.3`'s notes describe only what changed after `2.4.2` — the
  beta's own changes are not repeated. Worth editing the notes by hand in that
  case.
- The workflow refuses to run from anything other than `master`, and refuses to
  overwrite a tag that already exists.
- If it fails partway, nothing is half-published: the bump commit and the tag
  are pushed with `git push --atomic`, so both land or neither does.
